start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:keep-conversation-summaries with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_shop on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-shop-postgres-connection\"} and keep {\"app\": \"Email\", \"conversation_id\": \"Email:t1\", \"summary\": \"They ask for the Friday deck; I said yes.\", \"latest\": {\"id\": \"message:2\", \"at\": \"2026-10-19T10:05:00Z\"}}."
no_lists_because: It names no list: a conversation's summary is kept in the person's own store, in whatever form that store keeps things, and store says where and in which language.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the store is and how it is spoken to.
2. Say "Run workflow:keep-conversation-summaries" with store, and keep or remove as you want it done. keep needs the thread's latest message from the messages owner.
3. The first run makes the store's own objects once and proves them on the example attempts: every answer must be the one the intent says, or the run stops and says which.
4. To see whether a kept summary is stale, use tool:read-a-thread-summary with the record and the message times; it keeps nothing.

worked_examples.title: Keep a summary of an email thread
worked_examples.ask: Keep a summary of the Friday deck thread through its newest message.
worked_examples.given: The look step found no thread-summary object for Email:t1.
worked_examples.hands_back: written: a thread-summary object with summary_id thread-summary:Email:Email:t1 through message:2, at version 1.

store.where: postgresql database example_shop on my own computer

keep.summary: They ask for the Friday deck; I said yes.
